g.text: RT-01 Interior routing protocol: OSPFv2, single area 0
Why: Link-state OSPF converges quickly and, with few subnets and no Internet WAN, one area keeps
the database small enough that a full SPF run is trivial.
- multi-area OSPF: only 19 subnets; ABRs add config with no LSDB saving at this size
- EIGRP: Cisco-specific; OSPF is an open standard and the cloud edge cannot speak EIGRP
- static routes: no automatic failover; every new subnet needs edits on every router
Would change: Would split into areas at ≥ 50 subnets or with an Internet WAN.
RT-02 OSPF tuning on every router: auto-cost reference-bandwidth 10000, passive-interface default, point-to-point transit link
RT-03 Dual-homed failover: primary EVPL cost 10, backup cost 100, hello 1 s / dead 4 s
QOS-01 Latency target 5.0 ms: LLQ: DSCP EF (trading) in a 30% priority queue on every WAN edge
Choice: LLQ: DSCP EF (trading) in a 30% priority queue on every WAN edge (rule QOS.LAT)
Inputs: latency_target_ms=5, worst_link=hq↔remote-2, distance_m=35000 (35 km), trading_segments=2,
Why: Propagation, serialisation and processing are fixed by distance and hardware; only queuing
varies with load, so the latency target is protected by queuing policy.
